sections.text: Meditation is not for him who eats too much, not for him who eats not at all; not for him who is overmuch addicted to sleep, not for him who is always awake.
But for him who regulates his food and recreation, who is balanced in action, in sleep and in waking, it shall dispel all unhappiness.
When the mind, completely controlled, is centered in the Self, and free from all earthly desires, then is the man truly spiritual.

Unlike a car with its users manual, we are born without instructions how to live. We experience life vicissitudes without a so called users manual. The Gita has been described as such a guide. We obviously have been discussing the Yoga of Meditation. We went through several chapters with the Karma Yoga, then culminating the Karma into Wisdom and then Sannyasa Yoga. And now we are saying Dhyana Yoga, the Yoga of Meditation.
We have so far seen that all we are doing is for Atma Shuddhi -- the purification of my internal instrument. My mind and intellect are the internal instrument, and thats the only task I have as a seeker: to purify my mind and intellect so that my real self will shine through. Then I will realize who I am -- the peace which I had been seeking all my life.
Bhagavan said in the last verse we discussed that you will then achieve Shantim Nirvana Paramam Matsanstham Adhigacchati. In verse 15, it said: having gone through this Yoga of meditation -- how to control your mind, how to sit still, control your body, control your senses, control your mind, and then focus on yourself, focus on Me as your supreme goal -- you will find that peace which you had been looking for all your life. That peace resides in Me, the supreme self.
The peace Im seeking in this world does not exist in this world. And therefore me seeking the peace in this world is something like if, lets say for there is a one weekend at Kings Dominion, there is a free ride that you can take as many rides as many times, no tickets needed or no attendants are going to stop you from taking that ride over and over again. We go on that roller coaster ride because this is a great chance. I know its a lot of fun and here it is that there is no restriction. How many times I can take it. So I go on the roller coaster and while Im going through the roller coaster, Im constantly thinking, well, if this thing can stabilize, Ill really feel good about it.
Boy, it is going up and down. I cant even predict when its going to go up and when its going to come down. If it just stabilizes, Ill feel good about it. But because of my desire to have this fun, Im not getting off the roller coaster. And after all, I get so engrossed into this, I dont even realize when it stops and starts again. And Im constantly thinking, if this stabilizes, I may feel a little better about it.
At that point, some roller coaster guru can come and say, if you really want it stabilized, why dont you get off the roller coaster when it stops next time? So I said, what do I need to do? I said, well, just focus on when it stops. When it stops, you get out and then youll be in a stable ground, which is what your real place is on a stable ground. Thats where you were before. Before you decided you want to have this unlimited fun on this roller coaster.
Because there is no fee today. There is no restriction how many times you can take it. You say, well, Ill basically take it as long as I can stay there. But in that goal, I forgot that what Im seeking is stability. Thats my true nature. Thats what Im daily living.
But in that quest for getting this unlimited fun in what I always thought is a great fun, but I did not go there because it cost so much. Now that my chance to do it free, Im on a roller coaster constantly seeking for the stability which does not exist in roller coaster. Very nature of roller coaster is to go up and down. So some guru comes and said, just focus on yourself. When you see a little stability, thats where the roller coaster stops. And then you will find that stability which you had been seeking all throughout this roller coaster will be yours because it resides outside this roller coaster.
Bhagavan says the Santi Nirvana Paramam, that santhi which only gets when you are liberated from this rat of this limited being, trying to seek happiness and peace in this world outside. You will achieve that because your mind and intellect is now pure to experience the joy which resides in the self. And once you unite with that self, Matsangstham Adigacchati, you will achieve that state of mind. And then the last three verses which youve seen, which is 16, 17 and 18. And it said, what we tend to think is, well, I need to live my life as Im living. But then I need to have like 15 minutes in the morning.
Im going to meditate, you know, and then Ive achieved this state of paramshanti. Well that absolutely is a false notion. To do a meditation, you have to prepare for doing meditation. So how do we prepare for it? The Bhagavan says that the yoga is not possible for people who leave life without any control. I live undisciplined life.
And then I say, then I sit down and do yoga. A lot of people have this strong notion that I am living this dynamic life of working for 18 hours a day. But because I have 15 minutes of meditation then I can go on for another 18 hours. Bhagavan clearly says that thats not the reality. You live a life which is hectic and uncontrolled. You will not be able to meditate at all.
Therefore it says: Na ati ashnatah tu yoga asti -- for one who eats too much, Yoga is not possible. In other words, if Im indulging in sense gratifications, Yoga is not possible. It is also not possible for one who doesnt eat at all, who is completely avoiding any fulfillment for this body.
It clearly says that torturing my body and senses unnecessarily will not make me any more worthy of meditation than a person who lives a moderate, disciplined life. Na cha ati svapnashilasya -- one who is engaged in svapna (dreaming/sleeping).
Dreaming is only possible when youre sleeping. But I can be Svapnashila while Im waking in this world also, because from the point of Vedanta, the svapna extends from my dream world into the waking world. The waking world is nothing but another glorified dream from Vedantas perspective. Na cha ati svapnashilasya -- one who is sleeping too much, or not sleeping at all.
Jagrato naiva cha Arjuna -- or constantly awake in this world, more engaged in this world, not taking enough sleep. Anything which is extreme is to be avoided, because it will not give you the purity or the control over yourself to focus your mind.
Its very enlightening that this is not sacred knowledge you only learn from Bhagavad Gita. People learn this on their own when they want to achieve something. We say, Tomorrow I cannot do this because I have to wake up early. Im not coming to that party, Im not going to a late-night movie, if Im serious about what Im going to do the next day.
I saw two interviews on TV by two Bollywood stars whom I probably wouldnt think had ever gone to any school of philosophy -- both basically known for their good looks, like Akshay Kumar and John Abraham. In short interviews, the first thing they both said when asked how do you do that? was: I live a very disciplined life. You wouldnt expect to hear that from a Bollywood star, but both said the only way to achieve and maintain their stardom was by living a very disciplined life. I dont stay awake after 9 oclock or whatever.
I go to sleep by that time, I wake up early. Akshay Kumar said his show had to be recorded at six oclock in the morning -- that was the only time he would be available. He wont stay up late. He said, Im very disciplined.
I do this exercise daily. And I heard the exact same thing from John Abrahams interview somewhere. I wouldnt really think they have great knowledge of Bhagavad Gita or that somebody told them. They themselves figured out that the only way to maintain success is by living a disciplined life. Anyone who is serious about success eventually finds out that it is only possible through moderation. So Bhagavad Gita says, if Im not clear about that and think meditation will be a panacea that solves all my problems -- like saying I take Lipitor, so I can eat anything I want -- thats not a smart idea. Anytime a doctor gives me medication and says, Rajan, you have a cholesterol problem, heres the medication, the medication only works well if I also control my diet and make other lifestyle changes. In anything I want to achieve, moderation is the key. Bhagavan says, first of all, yoga is not for people who live an extreme life.
Then the positive message: Yukta Ahara Viharasya, Yukta Cheshtasya Karmasu, Yukta Svapnavabodhasya Yogo Bhavati Duhkhaha. Now you might ask: did I really forget why Im doing this yoga? Why did I start all this in the first place? If I have to live this moderate life and give up all the fun I used to have at parties at night, why do I even start? You are doing it, my friend, to get rid of your duhkha.
All the sorrows which you have, you want to get rid of them. Theres not a single moment in life where I can say, This pain is great, it really feels good. Unless youve heard this joke -- its pretty famous. Someone was banging his head against the wall.
Why are you banging your head against the wall? He said, because it feels good when I stop. Just to get that feeling of good. When you stop, you dont bang your head against the wall. You want to get rid of any pain that you have in your life, physical, mental, intellectual. You want to get rid of as quickly as possible in the easiest way.
Bhagavan says, Yukta Ahara Viharasya -- first, the person who is moderate in ahara, consumption of sense objects. Vihara means moving around, going on vacations, cruises. But sometimes that becomes more exhausting than work, doesnt it? Recreation also must be in moderation. I used to watch movies when I was a student because in those days that was the only entertainment -- sometimes three shows in a row: 12 to 3, then 3 to 6, then 6 to 9.

The Gitas teaching on moderation in these verses is remarkably practical and timeless. Naty-ashnatas tu yogosti na chaikantam anashnatah - yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who eats too little. The same applies to sleep, recreation, and all activities. This is not a call to austerity or self-denial, but to wisdom and balance. Interestingly, even successful Bollywood stars have discovered this principle through experience - that discipline and moderation are essential for sustained achievement.
We sometimes develop a dangerous misconception: I live a hectic 18-hour workday, but my 15 minutes of meditation will fix everything. This is like saying, I eat junk food constantly, but my daily vitamin will make me healthy. Bhagavan clearly states that an extreme, undisciplined life cannot be compensated by brief periods of meditation. The whole of life must become regulated - yukta-ahara-viharasya, yukta-cheshtasya karmasu - balanced in eating, recreation, and action.
The reward for this moderation is profound: Yogo bhavati duhkhaha - yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow. Why are we undertaking this practice? Not to punish ourselves, but to eliminate the suffering that pervades our lives. Today, honestly assess one area of your life that is out of balance. Are you sleeping too much or too little? Eating mindlessly or obsessively? Working to exhaustion or avoiding necessary tasks? Choose one small adjustment toward moderation. Remember: every aspect of life either supports or undermines your capacity for inner peace.
